items.followUp: A 50 kg cyclist experiences a forward force of 180 N and accelerates at 2 m s⁻². Find the friction force opposing the motion.

rubric.why: The resultant force is found from Newton’s second law.
rubric.how: Award for using F = ma and obtaining 120 N.

rubric.why: The applied force minus friction equals the net force; friction acts opposite the motion.
rubric.how: Award for obtaining 80 N and identifying its direction.

rubric.why: The answer must identify the requested force and its magnitude.
rubric.description: States the final force of friction.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the friction force is 80 N.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 40 kg, applied force = 200 N, a = 3 m s⁻².
Net force, F = ma = 40 kg × 3 m s⁻² = 120 N.
Applied force − friction force = net force.
Friction force = 200 N − 120 N = 80 N.
The force of friction is 80 N, opposite to the motion.

items.followUp: A force of 50 N makes an angle of 30° with the positive x-axis. Find its horizontal and vertical components.

rubric.why: Resolution means replacing one force by component forces along specified directions.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that a force is split or resolved into components along specified directions.

rubric.why: The horizontal component is adjacent to the angle θ.
rubric.how: Award for stating Fₓ = F cos θ.

rubric.why: The vertical component is opposite to the angle θ.
rubric.how: Award for stating Fᵧ = F sin θ.

modelAnswer: Resolution of forces is the process of splitting a force into component forces along specified directions.
For a force F making angle θ with the positive x-axis, the horizontal component is Fₓ = F cos θ.
The vertical component is Fᵧ = F sin θ.

items.followUp: A boat travels steadily at 6 m s⁻¹ against a water resistance of 2500 N. Calculate the power of its engine.

rubric.why: At steady speed, the resultant force is zero, so the engine force balances the water resistance.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the engine force is 4000 N because it balances the resistance.

rubric.why: For motion at constant speed, power is force multiplied by velocity.
The force and speed must be substituted into the power relation.
rubric.how: Award for showing the substitution of 4000 N and 4 m s⁻¹.

rubric.why: The calculated power is 16000 W, equivalent to 16 kW.
rubric.description: Gives the engine power with a unit.
rubric.how: Award for either equivalent final answer.

modelAnswer: Given: v = 4 m s⁻¹, water resistance = 4000 N.
Since the boat moves at steady speed, the engine force balances the water resistance: F = 4000 N.
Power, P = Fv.
The power of the engine is 16000 W (16 kW).

items.followUp: A wire 2 m long and of cross-sectional area 4 × 10⁻⁵ m² extends by 2 mm under a force of 8000 N. Find its Young’s modulus.

rubric.why: The extension must be converted to metres before calculating strain.
rubric.description: Expresses the extension in SI units.
rubric.how: Award for converting 1 mm to 0.001 m.

rubric.why: Young’s modulus is stress divided by strain, equivalently FL/(AΔL).
Correct substitution and evaluation give the modulus.
rubric.description: Substitutes the data and calculates Young’s modulus.
rubric.how: Award for correct substitution leading to 2 × 10¹¹.

rubric.why: Young’s modulus is measured in pascals, equivalent to N m⁻².
rubric.description: Gives the modulus with its SI unit.
rubric.how: Award for stating the final value with Pa or N m⁻².

modelAnswer: Given: L = 1 m, A = 5 × 10⁻⁵ m², F = 10000 N, ΔL = 1 mm = 0.001 m.
Young’s modulus, Y = stress/strain = (F/A)/(ΔL/L) = FL/(AΔL).
Y = 2 × 10¹¹ N m⁻².
Young’s modulus of the wire is 2 × 10¹¹ Pa.

items.followUp: What is a stopwatch? State the least count of a mechanical stopwatch.

rubric.why: A stopwatch is used to measure elapsed time or time intervals.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a stopwatch measures time intervals.

rubric.why: The least count of a mechanical stopwatch is one tenth of a second.

modelAnswer: A stopwatch is an instrument used to measure time intervals.
The least count of a mechanical stopwatch is 0.1 s.

items.followUp: A rectangular sheet is 8.4 cm long and 3.2 cm wide. Calculate its area to the appropriate number of significant figures.

rubric.why: The area of a rectangle is length multiplied by width.
rubric.how: Award for multiplying the given dimensions and obtaining 38.19 cm².

rubric.why: Both measurements have two significant figures, so the area must be rounded to two significant figures.
rubric.description: Rounds the area appropriately and gives its unit.
rubric.how: Award for 38 cm² to two significant figures.

modelAnswer: Given: length = 6.7 cm, width = 5.7 cm.
Area = length × width = 6.7 cm × 5.7 cm = 38.19 cm².
Both measurements have two significant figures, so area = 38 cm² to two significant figures.
